# Jānis Ruško (Janis Rusko)

Jānis Ruško is a senior expert in chemical risk assessment at BIOR in Riga, Latvia. His current work spans evidence synthesis, exposure assessment, risk prioritisation and European scientific cooperation. Analytical chemistry is an earlier technical foundation, not his current practice.

Current research: https://janisrusko.github.io/research.html
Professional record: https://janisrusko.github.io/work.html
Speaking and teaching record: https://janisrusko.github.io/speaking.html
Selected publications with DOIs: https://janisrusko.github.io/work.html#publications

## How the work connects

- Synthesise: monitoring data, consumption data, toxicological values and the literature, with sources and limits in view.
- Assess: exposure, risk-benefit trade-offs and uncertainty.
- Build: databases and tools that others can rerun and check.
- Communicate: the reasoning, for risk managers, specialists, students and the public.

## Current research

From Data to Decisions (July 2025 to June 2028), research application 1.1.1.9/LZP/1/24/124, co-financed by the European Regional Development Fund: he leads a postdoctoral project at BIOR building a transparent, auditable tool that ranks chemical risks in food. The tool links occurrence data reported to EFSA and BIOR's national results with food consumption data (EFSA's comprehensive database, by country and population group) and toxicological values (EFSA's first, from OpenFoodTox and its opinions; weaker sources are labelled). It harmonises units, takes results below the limit at the reported limit (lower, middle and upper bound), flags implausible values without dropping them, sums dietary exposure over the whole diet per substance and population group, and ranks substances on one concern scale (hazard quotient or margin of exposure) with a censoring band. Every gap is recorded and published as a gap map: substances without a toxicological value, foods missing from the consumption data, and foods eaten but never measured. Every method choice is a switch with a documented default, explained in the tool. Latvia is the first test case. Status at the end of October 2026: the engine and the interactive tool are built; the engine is being checked against EFSA's published exposure estimates, and results for named substances stay off public pages until that check passes. A public dashboard, an open-source release and a paper on the tool are planned. Related work: a joint review on risk classification and prioritisation methods with the University of Maribor (research stay, 11 May to 7 June 2026), and Occurrence Router, a separate tool for extracting occurrence data from scientific literature.

Project: https://bior.lv/en/projekts/the-scientific-institute-bior-in-cooperation-with-the-latvian-council-of-science-lcs-is-implementing-the-research-application-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-from-data-to-decis/
Progress: https://bior.lv/en/project-news/updates-on-project-no-1-1-1-9-lzp-1-24-124-for-the-period-from-2-january-2026-to-30-june-2026/

## Selected research

- Fish consumption: first author of the 2026 pilot risk-benefit assessment of Latvian inland fish, connecting contaminant exposure and nutritional benefits to weekly-consumption guidance. Foods. https://doi.org/10.3390/foods15050901
- Bee-product contaminants: coordinates literature search, screening and data extraction within BeSafeBeeHoney, bringing occurrence evidence together across honey, pollen, bee bread, royal jelly and propolis. COST CA22105: https://www.cost.eu/actions/CA22105/ Related publication (co-author): Glyphosate in apiculture: occurrence patterns across honey, pollen, and beebread. Food Control, 2026. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.foodcont.2025.111649
- Non-target screening: first-author study using high-resolution mass spectrometry to investigate potentially hazardous chemicals in paper straws and food-contact materials. Food Additives & Contaminants: Part A, 2020. https://doi.org/10.1080/19440049.2020.1711969

## Background

His current practice is research-led chemical risk assessment and evidence synthesis. Earlier work included chemical risk-assessment casework and scientific opinions for Latvian authorities. He holds a PhD in Chemistry from the University of Latvia (2021), with research in non-target screening and high-resolution mass spectrometry. He is Latvia's alternate member of EFSA's Management Board, a COST Management Committee member for Latvia in BeSafeBeeHoney and Agrifood-OneAI (2026–2030), teaches food-safety risk assessment at Rīga Stradiņš University, the University of Latvia and Riga Technical University, and was a BTSF tutor in 2024–2025 on the programme on sampling and analysis of veterinary medicinal products for officials from non-EU countries.

## Speaking and teaching

The selected record runs from 2017 to the present and spans public conversations, scientific conferences, institutional exchanges, recurring university teaching and international professional training. A featured public appearance was “Domā lēni par riskiem” at the Conversation Festival LAMPA on 21 June 2025. The most recent entries are a talk on the risk-benefit assessment of Latvian lake fish at the EIFAAC International Symposium in Riga (6 October 2026), a talk at Medilink Day in Riga (2 October 2026), food-risk outreach with his risk-assessor card game at the Latvian Council of Science Science Bubble in Mērsrags (15 August 2026) and at BIOR's stand at Researchers' Night 2026 and a Latvian Television interview on food safety in Latvia (Vides fakti, May 2026). Other 2026 entries include a presentation on glyphosate occurrence in honey, pollen and bee bread at the 3rd BeSafeBeeHoney Conference in Tirana (May 2026) and a lecture at the BeSafeBeeHoney Training School in Zagreb (July 2026). Earlier entries include a talk on experimental designs in analytical method development at a University of Latvia interdisciplinary research meeting (2017), a pitch on biosensing devices for organophosphate pesticides at EFSA's Risk Assessment Research Assembly in Utrecht (2018), a talk on non-target screening of paper food-contact materials at the University of Latvia 77th International Scientific Conference (2019), BETA talent seminars for secondary-school pupils (2019 and 2020), and a project-results briefing on chemical pollution around industrial sites for the State Environmental Service of Latvia (2021). Teaching includes guest lectures at the University of Latvia since 2018 and risk-assessment lectures for Rīga Stradiņš University nutrition students. The list excludes attendance-only events, duplicate presentation versions and co-authored posters where personal delivery is unclear. A map on the page shows talks, teaching, research stays, meetings and conferences across 23 countries, including the EU-FORA training trips from Naples in 2017 to 2018 (AGES Vienna, BfR Berlin, EFET Athens, EFSA Parma, and the Risk Assessment Research Assembly in Utrecht).

## Broader professional record

- Earlier chemical risk-assessment casework for Latvian authorities, beginning in 2018 and no longer part of his current practice.
- Drinking-water derogation assessments and leadership of a national risk-assessment and monitoring toolkit covering more than 200 parameters.
- Risk-benefit research on fish consumption through SEAwise and GreenAgroRes.
- Method development in non-target HRMS, anticoccidial residues, food phenolics, honey authenticity and multi-enzymatic biosensors.
- Accredited laboratory analysis at BIOR (2015–2017) in gas- and liquid-chromatography services.
- EFSA EU-FORA fellowship at CNR Naples (2017–2018): laboratory research on an automated multi-enzymatic biosensor for organophosphate pesticides, pitched at EFSA's Risk Assessment Research Assembly in 2018; later non-target screening collaboration with the US FDA.
- Recurring university teaching, thesis supervision, journal peer review and former European Commission BTSF tutoring.
- Former Alternate Member of the EFSA Focal Point Network (2021–2022) and participation in European expert groups and scientific fora.

## Collaboration

Welcomes collaboration on combining contaminant-occurrence datasets, extracting literature evidence, and developing dietary-exposure and risk-prioritisation methods, particularly projects connecting laboratories, research groups and public risk-assessment institutions. Contact through LinkedIn.
